headline: Town boards clashed over Special Town Meeting warrant articles, while Neary School plans narrowed and Costco hearings began.
synopsis: Southborough boards spent September preparing for the October Special Town Meeting, with the Select Board and Advisory Committee splitting sharply over Community Preservation Act funding for golf course irrigation and a trail footbridge, as well as two-family zoning amendments. The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed its focus for the Neary School project, voting to eliminate an exterior addition option in favor of courtyard or baseline renovation approaches. The Planning Board opened public hearings for a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-pump gas station at 21 Coslin Drive amid resident traffic concerns. Across municipal departments, officials began modeling dual FY28 budget scenarios, evaluating potential service and staffing cuts under a zero-growth scenario in the event of an override failure. Meanwhile, regional school committees approved a $22,750 market salary adjustment for the superintendent and paused a planned high school cell phone tracking app.

top_items.title: Neary School building committee eliminates exterior addition option
top_items.why: The committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 and directed consultants to focus on Options 1, 3, and a $15 million baseline.
top_items.body: Preliminary cost estimates presented to the Elementary School Building Committee ranged from $24.4 million to $49.2 million across various designs. Committee members voted to eliminate Option 4 due to complex soil conditions and site costs, instructing architects to concentrate future design and cost analysis on Option 1, Option 3 (enclosing the courtyard for a gymnasium), and an analysis of a $15 million scope baseline.

top_items.title: Planning Board opens review for Route 9 Costco project
top_items.why: Costco presented initial plans for a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-pump fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive.
top_items.body: The Planning Board opened public hearings on major site plan approval and special permits for the 26.12-acre project spanning the Southborough and Westborough town line. Residents and board members raised concerns regarding regional traffic congestion on Route 9, truck turnarounds at Route 85, cut-through traffic along Flagg Road, and stormwater management. The public hearing was continued to October 19.

top_items.title: Departments model cuts amid projected FY28 budget shortfall
top_items.why: Facing a projected $2 million deficit, departments prepared dual budgets with level-service and zero-growth options.
top_items.body: Under town guidance anticipating a spring Proposition 2 1/2 override vote, municipal departments drafted two FY28 budgets. While Request A maintains level services with 5 percent wage adjustments, Request B models zero growth and would require reductions in department hours, staff time, and operating expenses. The Board of Health and Conservation Commission expressed concern over the operational impacts of zero-growth cutbacks on small departments.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee rejects CPA funding for golf irrigation
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against Article 3, while the Select Board and CPC recommended approval.
top_items.body: Special Town Meeting Article 3 seeks an additional $433,546 in Community Preservation Act funds and $100,000 from the Golf Course Revolving Fund to replace the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system, raising total project funding to $1,087,296. While the Community Preservation Committee supported the request 4-1 and the Select Board voted 5-0 to recommend approval, the Advisory Committee unanimously opposed it, arguing the golf course should fund improvements through user fees rather than town CPA funds.

top_items.title: Town boards oppose CPA funding for Peninsula Trail bridge
top_items.why: The Select Board and Advisory Committee both voted against recommending $217,318 in supplemental CPA bridge funds.
top_items.body: The Trails Committee sought supplemental Community Preservation Act funding to construct a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian footbridge along Route 30 to connect Peninsula Trail sections, bringing total authorized funds to $428,550. While supported by the Community Preservation Committee, the Select Board voted 1-4 and the Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against recommending the appropriation, citing high per-foot construction costs during a tight fiscal period.

top_items.title: Zoning proposal for two-family dwellings advances to Town Meeting
top_items.why: The ZBA and Select Board backed amending two-family zoning rules, but the Advisory Committee recommended against it.
top_items.body: Article 2 on the Special Town Meeting warrant proposes eliminating the mandatory two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings and allows two-family dwellings by special permit. The Zoning Board of Appeals finalized text edits and the Select Board voted to recommend approval. However, the Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending the article over neighborhood density and septic capacity concerns, and the Planning Board continued its hearing to October 17.

top_items.title: School committees approve superintendent salary raise and pause app
top_items.why: Committees approved a $22,750 base salary adjustment for Superintendent Martineau and paused a high school cell phone tracking app.
top_items.body: The four regional and local school committees voted to increase Superintendent Gregory Martineau's base salary from $247,463 to $270,213, retroactive to July 1, 2026, as a market adjustment funded within existing budgets. Separately, Algonquin Regional High School administration announced a pause on implementing the Doorman geofencing mobile app for student phone restrictions, citing technical delays and community privacy concerns while continuing to use in-room caddies.
